translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise through Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, beloved son: grace and mercy and peace from God the Father and from Christ Jesus our Lord. (1)
I give thanks to God, whom I have served from the beginning with a pure mind, as I unceasingly hold the remembrance of you in my prayers night and day,
and I long to see you (those tears of yours come to my mind), so that I may be filled with joy.
I recall the unfeigned faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice; and I believe that it is in you as well. For it will dwell in you too.
For this reason I remind you to rekindle fervently the grace of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God has not given us a spirit of fearfulness, but of power and of love and of purity.
Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me, this prisoner of his, but share in suffering for the gospel by the power of God,
who saved us and called us with that holy calling, not because of our works, but by his own will and grace, which was given to us through Christ Jesus before those eternal times,
which has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior Jesus Christ, who abolished death and brought to light life and incorruption through the gospel,
for which I have been appointed a preacher, an apostle and a teacher of the Gentiles.
For this reason I also suffer these things, but I am not ashamed. For I know whom I have believed, and I believe that he is able to guard what I have entrusted to him until that coming day.
Hold as a pattern the word of life that you heard from me, in the faith and love of Christ Jesus.
Guard the good deposit by the Holy Spirit, who has dwelt in us. (2)
You surely know this, that all who are in Asia have abandoned me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus, for many times he refreshed me, and he was not ashamed of this chain of mine;
but he came to Rome and diligently searched for me and found me.
May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day; and how much he served me in Ephesus, you know better.
But you, my son, be strengthened by the grace of Jesus Christ,
and what you heard from me with many witnesses, entrust this to faithful men, who will be able to teach others as well.
Therefore endure hardship, as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No soldier entangles himself in the affairs of the world, so that he may please the commander.
And if anyone also competes, he is not crowned unless he competes lawfully.
The laboring farmer of the land ought to be first to receive of the fruit.
Understand what I am telling you. For the Lord will give you understanding in everything.
Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, of the line of David, according to my gospel,
in which I suffer evil even to the point of bonds, as an evildoer; but the word of God is not bound.
For this reason I endure everything for the sake of the elect, so that they too may find life through Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
The word is trustworthy: for if we die with him, we shall also live with him.
If we endure, we shall reign with him; if we deny him, he too will deny us.
If we do not believe, he remains faithful; he cannot deny himself.
Remind them of this before God and charge them not to dispute with words, which is of no use and only serves to subvert those who listen.
Strive to present yourself as chosen before God, a worker without shame, who rightly directs the word of truth.
But keep away from those foul and empty voices, for they advance further and further in lawlessness,
and their word finds pasture like gangrene; among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
who have departed from the truth, saying, "The resurrection has already happened," and they overturn the faith of some.
But the firm foundation of God stands, and it has this seal: "The Lord knows those who are his." And: "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord keep away from falsehood."
In a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and of clay, some for honor and some without honor.
If anyone cleanses himself from these, he will be an honorable vessel, pure from everything and useful to the Lord, prepared for every good work.
But flee the desires of youth, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord with a pure heart.
But abstain from foolish and uninstructed inquiries, knowing that they give birth to disputes.
And a servant of the Lord must not dispute, but must be quiet and kind toward all, a teacher, blameless,
peacefully teaching those who oppose him, in the hope that the Lord may perhaps grant them repentance, so that they come to know the truth,
and that they may beware of the snare of the devil, they who have been hunted by him according to his will.
But know this: in the last days evil times will come.
And people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful [?], arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to father and mother, ungrateful, unworthy, unloving,
not offering sacrifice [?], slanderers, impatient, unrestrained, implacable, untamed, haters of what is good,
betrayers, reckless, puffed up, lovers of desire rather than lovers of God.
They will have the form of godliness but deny its power. Keep away from these as well.
For among them are those who enter houses and take women captive, women bound up in sin, who acquire desires of various kinds,
and who are always learning and are never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these also oppose the truth, men corrupted in mind, untested in faith.
But they will not advance further, for their folly will be plain to all, as theirs also was. 7
But you have followed my teaching, zeal, faith, long-suffering, love, patience,
the persecutions and sufferings, how many befell me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra; how many persecutions I endured, and from them all the Lord delivered me.
And all who wish to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
But wicked men and sorcerers will advance to what is worse, deceiving and being deceived.
But you, stand firm in what you have learned and believed, knowing from whom you learned it;
And because from childhood you have known the divine books, which are able to make you wise for salvation through the faith of Christ Jesus.
Every book of God is spiritual and profitable for teaching and for reproof and for correction and for instruction in righteousness,
so that the man of God may be ready now, strengthened for every good work.
I testify before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead, according to his appearing and his kingdom.
Preach the word, persist in season and out of season, reprove, rebuke, and comfort, with all longsuffering and teaching.
For there will be a time when they will not accept the teaching of this life, but according to their own desire they will gather teachers for themselves, with itching of the ears;
and they will turn their hearing away from the truth and turn to fables.
But you, be watchful in everything, endure evil, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry well. [?]
For I am now being offered up, and the time of my departure has come.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
From now on that crown of righteousness awaits me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day; and not only to me, but to all who have loved his appearing.
Hasten to come to me soon,
for Demas has left me, having loved this world, and has gone to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia. Luke alone is with me.
Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
Send Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the cloak that I left in Troas with Carpus, and also the books, and above all the parchments.
Alexander the smith did me much evil. May the Lord repay him according to his deeds.
Beware of him yourself as well, for he strongly opposed our words.
At my first defense no one stood with me, but all abandoned me. May it not be counted against them.
But the Lord stood with me and strengthened me, so that through me the preaching might be fulfilled and all the Gentiles might hear it, and I escaped from the mouth of the lion.
And the Lord delivered me from every evil deed and will save me in his heavenly kingdom; his is the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet Priscilla and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
Hasten to come before winter. Eubulus and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers greet you.
The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with us. Amen.
